definitions.explanation: A flat, even area of land without significant elevation changes. Contrasts with mountains, hills, or uneven terrain.

examples.japanese: {平地|へいち}に{家|いえ}を{建|た}てる。
examples.english: To build a house on flat land.

examples.japanese: この{辺|あた}りは{平地|へいち}が{少|すく}ない。
examples.english: There is little flat land around here.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}は{山|やま}が{多|おお}く、{平地|へいち}は{国土|こくど}の{約|やく}{三|さん}{割|わり}しかない。
examples.english: Japan has many mountains, and flat land makes up only about 30% of the country.

notes:
Flat, level ground without significant elevation changes.

FORMS:
{平|へい} (flat) + {地|ち} (ground/land)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {平地|へいち}に{建|た}てる: to build on flat land
- {平地|へいち}が{少|すく}ない: little flat land
- {平地|へいち}を{走|はし}る: to run on flat ground

RELATED WORDS:
- {平野|へいや}: plain (a broad geographic region of flat terrain)
- {高地|こうち}: highlands
- {低地|ていち}: lowlands
- {山地|さんち}: mountainous terrain

SIMILAR WORDS:
{平地|へいち} emphasizes the quality of being flat, while {平野|へいや} refers to a named geographic region. Japan is about 70% mountainous, making {平地|へいち} a relatively limited and valued resource.
